claim.claim-text: 1. A virus-specific T cell composition comprising antigen-specific T cells that target antigens from human parainfluenza virus type 3 (PIV3), wherein the antigens from PIV3 comprise matrix protein (M), hemagglutinin-neuraminidase glycoprotein (HN), and nucleoprotein (N), optionally wherein the antigens from PIV3 further comprise fusion protein (F).

2. A virus-specific T cell composition comprising antigen-specific T cells that target antigens from human metapneumavirus (hMPV), wherein the antigens from hMPV comprise a combination of fusion protein (F), nucleoprotein (N), M2-1 protein (M2-1), and matrix protein (M).

3. The virus-specific T cell composition of claim 1 or 2 for use in a method of adoptive T-cell therapy, optionally for preventing or treating a viral infection, further optionally following hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT).
4. The virus-specific T cell composition of claim 1 or 2, wherein the virus-specific T cell composition is generated by a method comprising:

(i) establishing a hierarchy of immunodominance of virus antigens, comprising the steps of: (a) exposing peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) obtained from a pathogen exposed individual to two or more antigens from a virus in an in vitro culture in the presence of at least one Th-1 polarizing cytokine under conditions to allow T cells in the PBMCs that recognize the antigens to multiply in quantity to produce expanded T cells, (b) splitting the expanded T cells into a plurality of separate cultures and adding one of said antigens into each of the separate cultures, (c) measuring the magnitude of a biological response that results from the addition of each respective antigen to each of the separate cultures, (d) determining a level of unspecific response as a threshold value by measuring the magnitude of a biological response against an irrelevant target not expressed by the virus or against an unmanipulated PBMCs, (e) comparing the magnitude of the biological response from each of the separate cultures to the threshold value to discriminate expanded T cell cultures that are responders from expanded T cell cultures that are non-responders, (f) identifying expanded T cell cultures as responders if the biological response in step (e) exceeds the threshold value and identifying expanded T cell cultures as non-responders if the biological response in step (e) does not exceed the threshold value, (g) performing the same method using PBMCs obtained from multiple individuals, and for each of the two or more antigens from a virus, determining the frequency, relative to the number of individuals evaluated, that the expanded T cell cultures are responders and the frequency, relative to the number of individuals evaluated, that the expanded T cell cultures are non-responders, and (h) establishing a hierarchy of immunodominance of the antigens based on the mathematical formula: % of responders + 1 × magnitude of biological response % of non-responders + 1 ;
and

(ii) incubating PBMCs from a patient with libraries of peptides in the presence of one or more cytokines to generate the virus-specific T cell composition, wherein the libraries of peptides each comprise peptides corresponding to at least two immunodominant virus antigens identified in step (i).

5. The virus-specific T cell composition of claim 4, wherein the one or more cytokines are selected from the group consisting of IL4, IL7, IL12, IL21, IL15, IL6, and a combination thereof, optionally wherein the one or more cytokines comprise IL4 and IL7.

6. The virus-specific T cell composition of claim 4 or 5, wherein the biological response comprises production of one or more effector molecules selected from the group consisting of IFNγ, IL2, Granzyme B, GM-CSF, and TNFα.

7. A composition comprising an ex vivo expanded, donor-derived, polyclonal population of CD4+ and CD8+ virus-specific human T cells (VSTs) reactive against multiple antigens from human PIV3, wherein the multiple antigens from PIV3 comprise M, HN, N, and optionally F.
8. The composition of claim 7, wherein at least one or a combination of the PIV antigens are immunodominant antigens to human T cells, optionally wherein:

9. A composition comprising an ex vivo expanded, donor-derived, polyclonal population of CD4+ and CD8+ virus-specific human T cells (VSTs) reactive against multiple antigens from hMPV, wherein the multiple antigens from hMPV comprise F, N, M2-1, and M.
10. The composition of claim 9, wherein at least one or a combination of the multiple hMPV antigens are immunodominant antigens to human T cells, optionally wherein:

11. The composition of any one of claims 7-10, wherein the VSTs comprise T cells reactive to one or more libraries of peptides comprising peptides that overlap in sequence to span part or all of the multiple antigens.

12. The composition of claim 11, wherein the peptides are at least 7 amino acids in length and overlap by at least 3 amino acids, optionally wherein the peptides are each 15 amino acids in length and overlap by 11 amino acids.
13. The composition of claim 11 or 12, wherein the peptides span the entire length of each of the multiple antigens.
14. The composition of any one of claims 11-13 for use in a method of treating a subject at risk of or susceptible to viral infection, optionally following hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT).
15. The composition of any one of claims 11-13 for use in adoptive T-cell therapy.
